intro: To add a sheet in Numbers on Mac, click the plus button at the left end of the sheet tab row. Or press Shift-Command-N, which Apple lists as the shortcut for a new sheet.
tldr: Click the plus button at the left end of the sheet tab row to add a sheet.
Press Shift-Command-N, or ⇧⌘N, to do the same thing from the keyboard.
Add a table instead when the new data belongs on the current sheet.

blocks.text: A sheet is the top-level page in a Numbers document. Each sheet has its own canvas, and each one gets its own tab in the row along the top. People usually add a sheet when a new topic needs its own space, such as a new month, a client or a project. Adding one takes seconds. Deciding where it goes takes longer, so plan the layout before you add a dozen of them.
Use the plus button in the sheet tab row

Look at the top of your spreadsheet window. A row of sheet tabs runs along it. At the left end of that row sits a plus button. One click adds a new sheet to the row. The new sheet becomes the one you see, so you can start typing right away.

The mouse or trackpad suits you when you want to see the whole file. The keyboard suits you while you are typing into a table, because you do not have to lift your hands. Both routes end in the same place, a new sheet in the tab row.
Use the keyboard shortcut Shift-Command-N

Apple lists Shift-Command-N as the shortcut for a new sheet in Numbers for Mac. In Apple's symbols that is ⇧⌘N. Hold Shift and Command, then press N. The shortcut does the same job as the plus button, and it keeps the pointer where it is.
Sheet or table: pick the right one

Sheet and table cause most of the confusion around this task. A sheet is the page-sized canvas with its own tab. A table lives on a sheet and holds rows and columns of data. Ask yourself whether the new material is a separate topic or more data on the same topic.

rows: A separate topic, such as a new month
More data on the topic you are already working on
Table button on the current sheet
blocks.caption: Sheet or table? Pick by topic, not by size.

blocks.text: For the table side of that choice, read [How to add a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/add-a-table-in-numbers). It covers the Table button, styles and resizing, which you will likely need once the new sheet is open.
Why a new sheet can beat one long table
One long table gets harder to read as it grows. Headers scroll out of view, and totals sit among the rows they describe. Splitting the work across sheets keeps each block small and easy to check.

Use a sheet for the question you are answering. A sheet called Q3 costs keeps that question in one place. You can still reference figures from other sheets in a formula, which [How to add a formula in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/add-a-formula-to-a-cell-in-numbers) explains.
A worked example: one sheet for each month

Say you keep a household budget in Numbers. You want one sheet for each month of the year. Click the plus button for the first month, then press Shift-Command-N for each month after that. Work through the calendar in order, so the tabs read like a timeline.

Name each sheet as you go. Names like Untitled pile up fast, and you will waste time hunting for the right tab later. A pattern such as the month and year, for example January 2026, keeps the row easy to scan.
The same approach works for a client list, a project plan or a set of quotes. One sheet per client keeps each set of numbers separate. A table on each sheet holds the details for that client.
Which Numbers version you have

Numbers updates through the Mac App Store. The App Store listing shows Numbers 15.4.2 as the current version, and it requires macOS 26.0 or later. Apple's Numbers User Guide for Mac says it covers Numbers 15.4. If your version differs, check the guide that matches your version before you follow the steps to the letter.

Older Macs cannot install the current release, so they stay on an earlier Numbers build. The steps here follow Apple's guide for Numbers 15.4. If your Mac runs an older system, read the labels on screen and look for a plus button in the same row.
Common mistakes when adding a sheet

items: Adding a table when you meant a sheet. A table sits inside the current sheet, so the data stays on the same page.
Pressing the shortcut while another app is in front. Click the Numbers window first, then press ⇧⌘N.
Ignoring tab order. Put sheets in the order you will read them, so the first tab is the first thing you see.
Adding many sheets with no naming plan. Pick one pattern, such as client name and year, and use it every time.
Hunting for a sheet command in the menu bar and trusting a guessed path. This page leaves out a menu path because the source did not confirm one.

blocks.text: Undo a sheet you did not mean to add

If you add a sheet by mistake, press Command-Z. Undo is the standard Mac command, and it reverses your last change. Check the tab row afterward so you know the extra sheet is gone. Then try again with the method you meant to use.

blocks.title: Keep the tab row readable
blocks.text: Long names push tabs out of view on a narrow window. Short names keep more tabs visible at once. Keep your pattern the same from the first sheet to the last.
Where Lazur fits in

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold Option and Command, then ask about anything on your screen. If you ask where the plus button is, Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. If you ask it to walk you through a task, Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.

Lazur does not click for you. It points, explains and answers out loud. You still press the plus button or the shortcut. That split helps when you are new to Numbers and want to learn the layout, not hand the work off.
Ask Lazur about the next control

After the sheet exists, the questions change. You might ask where the Table button is, or what a control does. Lazur circles the control on screen and explains it. For image steps, read [How to add an image in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/insert-an-image-in-numbers).
Next steps and shortcut lists

Apple's shortcut table covers much more than sheets. For a full set of keys, read [How to use keyboard shortcuts in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/use-keyboard-shortcuts-in-numbers). When the file is finished, [How to share a spreadsheet in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/share-a-spreadsheet-in-numbers) explains how to invite people or send a link.
Sources and check dates

Apple's keyboard shortcut page lists Shift-Command-N for a new sheet. The Mac App Store lists Numbers 15.4.2 with a minimum of macOS 26.0. Apple's Numbers User Guide for Mac says it covers Numbers 15.4. These pages were checked on 2026-11-07.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to add a sheet in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Press Shift-Command-N, shown as ⇧⌘N. Apple lists it in its keyboard shortcut table for Numbers for Mac.

faq.question: What is the difference between a sheet and a table in Numbers?
faq.answer: A sheet is the page-sized canvas with its own tab. A table sits on a sheet and holds rows and columns. Add a sheet for a new topic and a table for more data on the same topic.

faq.question: Where is the plus button for a new sheet?
faq.answer: It sits at the left end of the sheet tab row, along the top of the spreadsheet window. Click it once to add a new sheet.

faq.question: Do I need the latest macOS to add a sheet?
faq.answer: The Mac App Store lists Numbers 15.4.2 with a minimum of macOS 26.0. If your Mac is older, the menus and buttons may differ, so check the Numbers guide that matches your version.

faq.question: Why does this page not give a menu path for adding a sheet?
faq.answer: The source we checked did not confirm a menu path. We left it out rather than guess. The plus button and Shift-Command-N are the confirmed methods.

faq.question: Can Lazur add the sheet for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the plus button and guides you one click at a time, but it does not click for you. You press the button yourself.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Numbers only?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on your Mac. Hold Option and Command to ask about what is on screen, and Lazur answers out loud.

task: Add a new sheet to a spreadsheet in Numbers
appliesTo: Numbers for Mac 15.4 and later, on macOS 26.0 or later
requirements: A Mac running macOS 26.0 or later for the current Numbers release
Numbers for Mac open with a spreadsheet
Numbers 15.4 or later, to match the steps in Apple's guide

steps.name: Open your spreadsheet
steps.text: Open Numbers and open the spreadsheet you want to change. Look along the top of the window for the row of sheet tabs. You need that row in view to find the plus button.
steps.tip: If you are not sure which file is open, check the window title before you add anything.

steps.name: Find the plus button
steps.text: At the left end of the sheet tab row, find the plus button. It sits beside the existing tabs, not inside the page canvas. Click it once.
steps.tip: The plus belongs to the tab row. Clicking inside the canvas adds nothing to the tab row.

steps.name: Check the new sheet appears
steps.text: Numbers adds a new sheet to the tab row. The new sheet becomes the sheet you see, so the canvas now belongs to it. Confirm the new tab appears before you type anything.

steps.name: Or use the keyboard shortcut
steps.text: Press Shift-Command-N. Apple's keyboard shortcut table for Numbers on Mac lists this for a new sheet. Hold Shift and Command together, then tap N once.
steps.tip: Click the Numbers window first. Shortcuts go to the app in front.

steps.name: Start your content on the new sheet
steps.text: Click the new sheet's canvas and type, or use the Table button in the toolbar to place a table. A sheet can hold more than one table, so you can stack several on one tab.

troubleshooting.problem: The plus button is not where the steps say.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your Numbers version against Apple's User Guide, which covers 15.4. The layout may differ on other versions, so read the labels on screen before you click.
Make sure Numbers is the front app and its window is active. Click an empty part of the window, then press the shortcut again.

troubleshooting.problem: You added a table instead of a sheet.
troubleshooting.fix: Press Command-Z to undo. Then use the plus button for a sheet, and the Table button only when you want rows and columns on the current sheet.

troubleshooting.problem: Numbers will not update to the latest version.
troubleshooting.fix: The App Store lists Numbers 15.4.2 as current and requires macOS 26.0 or later. If your Mac runs an older macOS, you cannot install that release, so use the guide for your version.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot find a sheet command in the menu bar.
troubleshooting.fix: This page gives no menu path because the source checked did not confirm one. The plus button and Shift-Command-N are the confirmed ways to add a sheet.
